newsitem.title: USA: New benchmarking key to refiner success - analyst.
newsitem.headline: New benchmarking key to refiner success - analyst.

text.p: U.S. oil refiners, faced with continuing price volatility of crude and refined products, must redefine the meaning of competitiveness to stay afloat in coming years, a consultant told refinery executives Tuesday.
"A new view of the refinery is needed," Marty Setzer of consultantcy Price Waterhouse told executives attending the National Petroleum Refiners Association (NPRA) annual meeting.

Setzer noted the new changes must come on top of the benchmarking already spawned by the influential Solomon Study of U.S. refiner processing performance put out by Houston-based oil consultancy Solomon Associates Inc.

"To be successful in this new global environment a refiner must redefine his context of pacesetter performance," Setzer said, noting efficient internal conversion processes must now be wed to the volatile market outside of the refinery.
He stressed that while "volatility is here to stay," oil refineries exist to add value to crude oil, and executives should never lose sight of this simple fact.
Setzer said those outside factors included a product markets and distribution system, a global crude trading system, and a derivatives paper trading system.

"Successful refiners that have effectively defined and now operate in this new context have achieved as much as $0.25 to $0.75 a barrel (profit) improvement -- on top of the internal refinery improvements done as part of a traditional Solomon Study approach," Setzer said.
Setzer also emphasized success requires total understanding of the downstream, a trading mentality and a readiness to take advantage of global trading opportunities.
He also said refiners, apart from clearly articulating the overriding strategy from the top, must be willing to abandon a 'top-down' managerial approach in running their businesses.
Instead, they must "involve fresh people with fresh ideas," allowing bright employees and nimble teams of employees to execute the company's strategy in the most efficient manner.

He pointed to Tosco Corp as the refiner that is setting the downstream pace, noting the company has among other competitive advantages, a systems approach, a trading mentality and routinely makes quick decisions as to whether buying products or making them from crude is the most attractive economic opportunity.
